---
title: Style the cursor and the chat
description: "Give the agent your brand: one custom property recolours the cursor, its rings and the chat's accent, and a few more set the chat's surfaces, corners and typeface, in light and dark."
sidebar:
  label: 10. Style the cursor and the chat
---

The cursor and the chat ship with a neutral black look. Both are styled with **CSS custom properties**: you set a few
values in a stylesheet of your own and never touch their markup. The chat's accent follows the cursor's colour, so
one property, `--agent`, brands both.

## A complete example

One file holds the whole theme. The same file works in every framework.

<View title="Vite">

<include meta='title="src/agent.css"'>/_examples/shared/agent.css</include>

Import it in your entry file, with the two stylesheets you already have:

```tsx src/main.tsx
import "@webmcp-agents/core/cursor.css";
import "@webmcp-agents/chat/chat.css";
import "./agent.css"; // [!code highlight]
```

</View>

<View title="Next.js">

<include meta='title="app/agent.css"'>/_examples/shared/agent.css</include>

Import it in the root layout, with the stylesheets you already have:

```tsx app/layout.tsx
import "@webmcp-agents/core/cursor.css";
import "./globals.css";
import "./agent.css"; // [!code highlight]
```

</View>

<View title="TanStack Start">

<include meta='title="src/agent.css"'>/_examples/shared/agent.css</include>

Link it from the root route, with the stylesheets you already have:

```tsx src/routes/__root.tsx
import agentCss from "../agent.css?url"; // [!code highlight]

// In head(), in `links`:
{ rel: "stylesheet", href: agentCss }, // [!code highlight]
```

</View>

<View title="Astro">

<include meta='title="src/agent.css"'>/_examples/shared/agent.css</include>

Import it in your layout, with the stylesheet you already have:

```astro src/layouts/Layout.astro
---
import "@webmcp-agents/core/cursor.css";
import "../agent.css"; // [!code highlight]
---
```

</View>

Every selector in the file starts with `html`. The library's own rules are written on `:root` and `.wa-chat`, and
between two rules of the same weight the one that loads last wins, which depends on how your framework orders
stylesheets. The extra `html` makes yours heavier, so they win wherever the file is imported.

## The cursor

`--agent` is the agent's colour. The arrow and the name tag are filled with it, and everything else is worked out from
it: the focus ring and outlines, the soft fill of the ripple and the halo, the colour of the waiting state. Set the
others only when you want them to differ.

| Property | What it colours | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | The arrow and the name tag. | `#111111` |
| `--agent-ink` | The text on the name tag. | `#ffffff` |
| `--agent-strong` | The focus ring, the ripple's edge and the dashed outlines. | `--agent` |
| `--agent-wait` | The same parts while the cursor waits for the person's click. | `--agent` |
| `--agent-edge` | A thin light line around the ring and the ripple, so a dark agent shows on a dark page. | white at 60% |

Set them on the root element (`html:root`, as in the example). The soft fills are computed there, so `--agent` set
on a deeper element does not reach them.

The name in the tag is not CSS: it is the `name` option of the visuals
([`installAgentVisuals`](/reference/core/install-agent-visuals)). Motion is not yours to restyle either: the cursor
writes its own position every frame, and it already honours `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## The chat

The chat reads `--agent` for its accent: the launcher, the send button, the person's own messages, focus outlines. Its
other properties are set on its host element, `.wa-chat`:

| Property | What it sets | Default (light) |
|---|---|---|
| `--wa-chat-accent`, `--wa-chat-accent-ink` | The accent and the text on it, when the chat should not follow the cursor. | `--agent`, `--agent-ink` |
| `--wa-chat-bg`, `--wa-chat-fg` | The panel and its text. | `#ffffff`, `#111111` |
| `--wa-chat-muted` | Secondary text. | `#5f6368` |
| `--wa-chat-line`, `--wa-chat-soft` | Borders, and the fill of chips and tool calls. | black at 10% and 5% |
| `--wa-chat-radius` | The panel's corners. | `14px` |
| `--wa-chat-font` | The typeface. | the system font |
| `--wa-chat-gap` | The distance from the corner of the window. | `20px` |

To give the chat a different accent from the cursor (in light; [dark mode](#dark-mode) has its own):

```css src/agent.css
html .wa-chat {
  --wa-chat-accent: #0f766e;
  --wa-chat-accent-ink: #ffffff;
}
```

## Dark mode

The chat has a dark look of its own. It turns on with the system setting (`prefers-color-scheme`), or with
`data-theme="dark"` on the chat or any element around it; `data-theme="light"` keeps it light. So a site with its own
theme switch that writes `data-theme` on `<html>` needs nothing more.

The accent adapts by itself. On the dark panel it is a light tint of `--agent` with dark text on it: the default
near-black agent becomes a light grey, a brand blue a light blue. You do not set a second colour for dark.

What you changed on `.wa-chat` yourself applies in light only, since the chat's dark rules are heavier than
`html .wa-chat`. That goes for a surface (`--wa-chat-bg`, `--wa-chat-fg`) and for an accent of the chat's own. Give
each its dark partner, under the same condition the chat uses:

```css src/agent.css
html[data-theme="dark"] .wa-chat {
  --wa-chat-bg: #0f172a;
  --wa-chat-fg: #e2e8f0;
  --wa-chat-accent: #5eead4;
}
```

A site that follows the system setting instead wraps the same rule in `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`.

The cursor has no dark variant to switch: the arrow carries a white edge and the ring a light one, so it reads on
both.

## One part of the chat

Every part of the chat has a class that starts with `wa-chat__` (`wa-chat__launcher`, `wa-chat__panel`,
`wa-chat__header`, `wa-chat__bubble`, `wa-chat__composer`, `wa-chat__send`, `wa-chat__tool`). The stylesheet sits
outside any cascade layer and most of its rules are a single class, so a selector with `html` in front overrides
them:

```css src/agent.css
html .wa-chat__launcher {
  border-radius: 12px;
}
```

Prefer the properties where one exists: the class names are the chat's own markup and follow it when it changes.
A rule of the chat that is longer than one class (a part in one state, such as a docked panel) needs your selector
to name that state too. For a chat built from your own components instead, see [shadcn chat blocks](/more/shadcn-chat-blocks).

## Try it

Start the app and call a tool, from the chat or from the [devtools](/build/devtools). The arrow, its name tag and
the ring around the field it types into are in your colour, and so are the chat's launcher and send button. Switch
your system to dark: the chat's panel turns dark and its buttons take a light tint of your colour.

If nothing changes, the file is not loaded: check the import in the view above.

## Options you'll use most

| Property | Set on | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | `html:root` | The agent's colour, for the cursor and the chat's accent. |
| `--agent-ink` | `html:root` | Text on the name tag and on the chat's accent. |
| `--agent-strong` | `html:root` | Rings and outlines in another shade. |
| `--wa-chat-accent` | `html .wa-chat` | An accent for the chat alone; add a dark partner. |
| `--wa-chat-bg`, `--wa-chat-fg` | `html .wa-chat` | The chat's panel and text; add a dark pair. |
| `--wa-chat-radius` | `html .wa-chat` | The chat's corners. |
| `--wa-chat-font` | `html .wa-chat` | The chat's typeface. |

Every property, class and state: [`cursor.css`](/reference/core/cursor-css) and
[`<AgentChat>` theming](/reference/chat/agent-chat#theming).
